statements.impact_statement: Reassessed for pinned EJS 7.0.2 with epub-gen-memory 1.1.2. The reported attack requires attacker-controlled templates or compilation options. ProjectExporter constructs title/author/preset metadata explicitly; toEpub constructs a fixed generator-option allowlist and escapes manuscript text. The generator renders its packaged templates with data only. In EJS 7.0.2 lib/cjs/ejs.js, render(template, data, options) uses only its third argument for compilation options; data is not copied into options. No template body/path, closeDelimiter, client, escapeFunction or settings from export metadata reaches that argument. Regressions in tests/unit/services/manuscript-exporters.test.ts exercise template syntax as text and malicious template/engine-option properties while verifying real EPUB output; all nine exporter cases pass. Vendor security policy: https://github.com/mde/ejs/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Exact product version and CVE only; reassess on any generator, EJS, template or export-option change.

The Node runtime is constrained to ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1 by the shared runtime policy, checked again by the inventory producer. Node documents the Brotli decoder fix in these security releases despite process.versions.brotli retaining 1.2.0. The measured Node24.22.2 executable is recorded by SHA256. This disposition concerns Node-bundled Brotli, not standalone unpatched Brotli. https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases#nodejs-brotli-decoder-out-of-bounds-write-permits-remote-code-execution-cve-2026-111497---high

NVD matches without an appropriate modern V8 upper bound. The CVE concerns Node before0.12.6 / io.js before1.8.3/2.3.3; the measured V8 is bundled in supported Node24.22.2. https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2015-5380 and https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2015-security-releases . Exact V8 product version only; reassess other findings.

All affected copies are development-only Jest, TypeScript-ESLint and watcher dependencies. Patterns come from checked-in test/lint configuration and developer-selected paths; manuscript/MCP inputs cannot provide extglob expressions. npm lock dev-only status is enforced by the inventory producer. Evidence: npm ls picomatch --all and package-lock.json. Reassess any production use or untrusted pattern input.

The Marvin advisory concerns RustCrypto RSA private-key operations observable through timing. This binding exports asset inspection and signing through ClaimSigner (native/c2pa-binding/src/lib.rs), whose AsyncSigner implementation calls a JavaScript callback with bounded message bytes and receives only signature bytes. It never receives a private key. src/services/content-credentials/sdk-worker.ts decrypts encrypted PKCS8 into a Node KeyObject and createRawCredentialSigner performs RSA-PSS using node:crypto/OpenSSL with explicit PSS padding and digest-sized salt. Public verification remains in the SDK; no Rust RSA private-key decryption/signing operation is exposed. tests/unit/services/content-credentials-sdk.test.ts independently verifies real PSS callback signatures. Exact binding architecture and rsa 0.9.10 only; reassess if private keys or native signing are introduced. The dependency itself remains unpatched: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html .

The CNA describes predictable V8 string hash collisions in 2011-era engines. The measured Node 24.22.2 runtime uses V8 13.6.233.17-node.63. Its pinned source initializes the default hash seed from isolate.random_number_generator()->NextInt64() and supplies that seed to string hashing, rather than the historical predictable hash implementation: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.22.2/deps/v8/src/numbers/hash-seed.cc and https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.22.2/deps/v8/src/strings/string-hasher-inl.h . The raw CNA record and source snapshots are retained in the security follow-up evidence. Exact V8 product version in the supported default Node runtime only; not a general denial-of-service immunity claim.

The CNA record identifies V8 as used in Chrome before 15.0.874.102; the Chrome 15.0.874.102 release explicitly includes the fix. The measured product is modern V8 13.6.233.17-node.63 in Node 24.22.2, not that 2011 engine. This match results from the broad historical V8 CPE record. References: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2011/10/chrome-stable-release.html and https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2011-3886 . Exact V8 product version only; reassess other versions and advisories.
